note:
THAD STANDING, BREATHING, LOOKING UP at the driver's box.

THE BREATH TRANSFORM QUANTISES ITS OWN MIDDLE STEP AWAY at this figure height. It uses amp = 0.005*fig_h and step = round(fig_h/240), then rounds the offset to whole display pixels -- at 526 that is amp 2.6 and step 2, so t=0.5 and t=1.0 BOTH round to -2. The curve 0, .5, 1, 1, .5, 0 becomes two pictures and the breath pops rather than rising.

The same arithmetic produced sixteen two-picture clips across the project. A curve needs its intermediate values to survive the rounding: three real offsets need amp of at least 2*step*1.5, which at step 2 is 6, not 2.6. This clip uses amp 6 and a four-point rise.

The breath is the rig's own transform applied by hand, because character.py's hem detector requires two legs of roughly equal width sustained -- and a STANDING pose has them together, which is the whole point of it. Above 30% of figure height is still, so the head and collar never move; the coat rises and settles between there and the hem at y357; the legs are planted.

I first cut only the head, because I measured this generation against thad-stand-left and got 41% silhouette overlap below the collar. THE COMPARISON WAS THE WRONG WAY ROUND: thad-stand-left has his feet 100% of his width apart -- it is a WALKING pose, derived from a walking source, the same fault Hob's stand had. This generation has them together at 80%. It is a proper standing pose and the existing clip is not; I compared the good one to the bad one and blamed the good one.

He has no other art that looks up. Four facings, three talk overlays, none tilted -- which is why four rounds of 'the fix is positional' could never have worked.

LEFT, because the driver's own looking-down turns toward frame RIGHT: 107k changed pixels right of his head's centre against 51k left. Thad stands to the driver's RIGHT, facing left, looking up-left while the driver looks down-right.
stateNote: A STATE OF `idle`, NOT A CLIP OF ITS OWN. As {id: 'lookup'} nothing but a chore could play it, and a chore is a one-shot -- 6 frames at reactRate 7 is 0.86s, gone before the driver answers. As a state of the clip he already stands in, setState holds it for as long as a beat says. Q75. Added by hand because this clip predates character.py's --state; regenerating it through the rig would write both fields.
